items.title: Work–Life Balance and Employee Engagement in Commercial Banks in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between work–life balance and employee engagement among commercial bank officers in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Specifically, it investigated flexible work time, telecommuting, and leave policy in relation to physical, emotional, and cognitive engagement, while examining the moderating role of organisational culture. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, using a census approach to cover 114 banking offices across seven commercial banks. Of the 114 questionnaires distributed, 108 valid responses were obtained, representing a response rate of 94.7%. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rank-order correlation, and regression analysis in SPSS version 26. Reported Cronbach’s alpha coefficients ranged from .79 to .88. The findings indicated positive associations between all three work–life balance dimensions and the three dimensions of employee engagement. Leave policy had the strongest reported association with cognitive engagement (𝑟𝑠 = .646,𝑝 < .01). The regression results also indicated a significant interaction between work–life balance and organisational culture (𝛽 = .213,𝑝 = .004). The study concludes that work–life balance practices are positively associated with employee engagement in the study setting. It recommends improved leave administration, flexible scheduling where operationally feasible, role-appropriate telecommuting, and a supportive organisational culture.

items.title: Workplace learning and AI challenges: causes and effects
items.abstract: Purpose The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplaces is rapidly increasing in our society. This means that AI is fundamentally reshaping workplaces, how tasks are performed and how the authors interact with colleagues. This study aims to develop explanatory knowledge about the challenges of AI-augmented workplaces. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative and deductive research approach was applied. Key challenges discovered in the literature review were used as predefined themes to identify and analyse empirical data. Findings The authors have identified five key challenges: AI Strategy, AI Education, Control, Meaningfulness and Integrated Work Processes for Human-AI Collaboration. These challenges were examined in terms of their causes and effects, and an explanatory model (AICH) was developed. Research limitations/implications The study collected data from five companies, which provides some generality beyond this study’s empirical domain. However, it poses challenges in making broader generalisations. Future research could be designed as broader studies to confirm, modify or challenge the findings. Practical implications The findings contribute to workplace learning and provide a basis for identifying risks and potential measures. Social implications The identified challenges regarding AI-assisted workplaces will most likely have broader social ramifications, affecting employees’ overall well-being and company culture. Originality/value The authors do not claim that the challenges per se are new. However, the authors claim that the models consisting of explanatory knowledge visualised as cause-and-effect models are new.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

items.title: Wrongdoers or Saviors? CEO Activism, Media Partisanship, and the Media’s Construction of CEO Infamy and Celebrity
items.abstract: This study advances research on social evaluations by theorizing how partisan media construct CEO infamy through dramaturgical logics distinct from those underlying CEO celebrity. Moving beyond conceptualizations of infamy as merely negative celebrity, we argue that infamy emerges through simple melodramatic narratives casting CEOs as wrongdoers, whereas celebrity involves more complex dramatized narratives portraying CEOs as saviors. Focusing on CEOs’ liberal sociopolitical activism—a visible, ideologically-charged action that departs from conventional executive roles—we theorize that this behavior generates divergent constructions in partisan media: infamy in conservative outlets and celebrity in liberal outlets. We further argue that activism more readily generates infamy than celebrity because melodramatic narratives are simpler to construct and negative deviance is more readily perceived than positive deviance. We examine two moderators of these relationships. Firm performance differentially shapes these constructions, with poorer performance intensifying conservative-media infamy and stronger performance amplifying liberal-media celebrity. CEO social media engagement, conversely, attenuates both by constraining traditional media’s narrative discretion and reducing activism’s newsworthiness. We develop an LLM-based annotation system capturing CEO-directed sentiment, role attributions, and dramaturgical narratives in media articles. Analyzing 91,608 articles covering 705 S&P 500 CEOs across 45 ideologically polarized U.S. media outlets between 2016 and 2022, we find broad support for our hypotheses across our main and extensive supplemental analyses. Our findings advance understanding of CEO infamy and social evaluations more generally by revealing how partisan media construct divergent social evaluations of the same executive behavior through distinct narrative processes.

items.title: XAI as a Trust Calibration Mechanism in Teleoperated Human-Agent Systems: A Conceptual Framework
items.abstract: As teleoperated systems increasingly incorporate autonomous agents capable of independent decision-making, the human operator transitions from a direct controller to a delegated supervisor. This shift introduces a fundamental challenge: how operators calibrate their trust toward agents whose decisions they cannot interpret. Miscalibrated trust, whether overtrust leading to unsafe delegation or undertrust causing inefficient over-intervention, represents one of the most consequential human factors risks in agentic teleoperation. This paper argues that Explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms constitute a promising but underexplored lever for dynamic trust calibration in teleoperated human-agent systems. A three-layer conceptual framework is proposed that maps operator profiles to adaptive XAI modality selection and closes the loop through a trust feedback mechanism that dynamically adjusts the agent’s level of autonomy. Three application scenarios, namely robotic surgical assistance, hazardous environment inspection, and remote industrial maintenance, are examined to illustrate how the framework operates under realistic teleoperation constraints. The paper identifies key research challenges and outlines a forward-looking agenda for empirically grounding the proposed framework.

items.title: 'We just went with what seemed the best supported': Lessons on Cryptographic Practices in Securing Microcontrollers from Embedded CTFs
items.abstract: Microcontroller-based embedded systems support safety- and security-critical applications yet provide insufficient resources for modern cryptography. While numerous lightweight primitives and libraries have been proposed, little is known about how practitioners select and deploy them. We bridge this gap with a mixed-methods study of the 2023 and 2024 MITRE Embedded Capture-the-Flag (eCTF) competitions. We review 47 working firmware submissions and hold 22 semi-structured interviews with team members. Our analysis reveals two classes of findings. 1) General lessons echo broader usability and human-factors challenges observed in other domains: Developers favor speed and integration convenience over stronger security guarantees, and unclear documentation poses greater barriers to implementing cryptographic functionality than raw resource limits. 2) Embedded-specific lessons highlight unique challenges in resource-constrained environments: Side-channel hardening receives disproportionate attention compared to protecting data at rest, platform heterogeneity complicates portable privacy-preserving implementations, and limited debugging and verification support make it difficult to validate security properties at runtime. We group these findings into implementation practices, participant insights, and practical challenges while giving concrete advice for researchers, educators, device vendors, and the open-source community. Our results show how cryptography is applied in today's security-oriented embedded projects and outline near-term steps to make these systems safer and easier to build.

items.title: "It Scams In The Family:" GenAI Voice Cloning Scams among Sighted and Families with Blind or Low Vision Members
items.abstract: The usual victim in phone scams is an individual at risk of being defrauded or whose identity might be stolen. But a new scamming scheme has emerged, targeting families as victims instead - an individual at risk of being defrauded through an emergency request, voiced by a clone of a related individual whose voice identity has been non-consensually sampled. As these scams are harmful both to the well-being and individuals' true identity (voice), in addition to financial loss, we set to ''conceptually replicate'' an early exploration done by Sharevski et al. (2025) through naturalistically resembling experiences with n1=10 families involving sighted and n2=10 involving a blind or a low vision member (pairs of a 'caller' and 'callee', n=40 total). Our thematic analysis uncovered an overarching attitude of ''self-preparedness'' to withstand these scams, based on both 'intrinsic' motivation to ward off pressure to act on an emotional impulse and 'extrinsic' motivation to avoid immediate and long-term victimization. Expanding the original study's findings with the experiences of a population reliant on voice both as a medium and as an access, we draw on the resilience themes to sketch out 'user-sensitive' accessible designs against GenAI scams.

items.title: 3D-Sec '26: The 2nd ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security
items.abstract: The 2nd ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security (3D-Sec), co-located with ACM CCS 2026, brings together researchers and practitioners to address security challenges arising from AI-enabled misinformation, digital deception, and synthetic media. Advances in Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), multimodal generation, and adversarial machine learning have increased the accessibility and sophistication of deepfakes, synthetic personas, automated disinformation, and AI-assisted social engineering. These capabilities are increasingly relevant to impersonation, financial fraud, influence operations, cybercrime, and state-sponsored information operations, while also challenging existing approaches to detection, attribution, provenance, and mitigation. Addressing these threats requires interdisciplinary efforts spanning cybersecurity, multimedia forensics, artificial intelligence, human factors, and information integrity. 3D-Sec provides a dedicated forum for advancing research on the detection, analysis, attribution, and mitigation of AI-enabled deception and disinformation. The workshop aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, identify emerging security challenges, and advance practical approaches for strengthening trust and security in AI-mediated digital environments. Further information is available at: https://sites.google.com/view/3d-sec2026.

items.title: A closer look at case law reading: an empirical study of students’ case-reading habits, experiences and preferences
items.abstract: The skill of reading cases has always been pivotal to legal education in common law jurisdictions. However, case reading is not necessarily something that comes easily to law students or with which they readily engage. This article reports on an empirical study of case-reading habits, experiences and preferences of Juris Doctor students at the Law School at the University of Western Australia. Using self-determination theory, it argues that case reading is not only a skill but a practice shaped by class environments, learning materials and social conditions. It recommends approaches that strengthen students’ intrinsic motivation to read.

items.title: A Participatory Approach to Designing Low-Cost Ergonomic Equipment for Informal Food Vendors in Zimbabwe
items.abstract: In Sub-Saharan Africa, informal food vendors suffer from high levels of physical strain at work and are not engaged in workplace health promotion programs. In order to address this, the Authors conducted a study to determine the level of discomfort experienced by street food vendors in Harare and Bulawayo, and came up with some basic and cheap ergonomic solutions. A mixed methods participatory approach was implemented involving a baseline assessment (n=412) based on standard ergonomic tools, focus groups and co-design workshops, followed by a comparative evaluation (n=204). A $18.70 package was co-designed by vendors using local materials that includes an adjustable cooking platform, a padded load carrier, an anti-fatigue mat, and a peer led postural education program. Baseline assessment identified that 78.4% of vendors had high levels of physical strain, mainly in the lower back, neck and shoulders and 87.3% of tasks were identified as being at high postural risk. After 6 months of implementation, the prevalence of discomfort in the active group had reduced by 43.3% (34.2% less than in the control group; p<0.001). In addition, there were significant reductions in mean postural risk scores and improvements in work ability. This designed package has significantly lowered postural risk, physical strain and work ability, at just a small fraction of a month's median income. These can be effective, participatory, and community-based solutions that are accessible to the informal sector and can be an effective model for integrating occupational health support.

items.title: A saúde musculoesquelética de auxiliares de autópsia: fatores de risco ergonômicos e estratégias preventivas
items.abstract: The forensic and post-mortem examination environment imposes strenuous physical demands on technical support personnel, with the autopsy assistant playing a crucial operational role. The objective of this study is to examine the occupational and ergonomic risk factors associated with the development of musculoskeletal disorders among autopsy assistants, as well as to discuss effective ergonomic and organizational interventions to mitigate injuries. Methodologically, a narrative and exploratory literature review was conducted, supplemented by the analysis of the technical and operational dynamics intrinsic to body removal, transportation, cavity evisceration, and body reconstruction. The findings reveal that significant biomechanical strain on the lumbar spine, upper limbs, and peripheral joints results from manual patient handling, awkward and prolonged static postures, and repetitive cutting and suturing motions. It is concluded that the prevention of musculoskeletal disorders demands a comprehensive re-evaluation of ergonomic management within Institutes of Legal Medicine, requiring assistive lifting technologies, height-adjustable autopsy tables, continuous ergonomic training, and dedicated occupational health programs for forensic professionals.

items.title: AI AS A COGNITIVE ENHANCEMENT TOOL: A FOUR-TIER INSTRUCTIONAL MODEL FOR TEM-8 WRITING
items.abstract: The writing task in Test for English Majors Grade Eight (TEM-8) places high demands on learners’ ability to synthesize information and express critical perspectives. Drawing on teaching practice in the English Writing and Translating Skills Training course for English majors at a Double First-Class agricultural university, this study develops a four-tier model of AI-enhanced writing instruction, with the four tiers corresponding to four ascending levels of cognitive engagement: evaluative regulation, critical analysis, comparative discernment, and selective revision. Using ChatGPT and DeepSeek as supporting tools, the model treats AI as a tool for cognitive enhancement rather than a substitute writer. By analyzing the strengths and weaknesses of AI-generated essays, comparing outputs from different platforms, and using AI critically to revise their own work, students make a cognitive shift from passively receiving feedback to actively directing their use of the technology. This paper explains the rationale, key components, and implementation of the model, offering a replicable framework for integrating AI into writing instruction for English majors in higher education.

items.title: Algorithmic temporal governance: a sociotechnical theory of labor control, worker adaptation and resistance
items.abstract: Algorithmically mediated work systems are reshaping how organizations govern workers’ time. This paper develops the Temporal Sociotechnical Algorithmic Model (TSAM), a sociological theory explaining how computationally mediated information asymmetries alter workers’ capacity to anticipate, allocate, withhold, and collectively contest their labor time. Drawing on a critical interpretive synthesis of 56 peer-reviewed publications identified through a structured search covering 2000–2024, TSAM begins from a generative condition in which labor time becomes an optimizable organizational resource while workers retain only partial visibility into the processes governing allocation, availability, and evaluation. From this condition, the model specifies three system-level mechanisms: unpredictability, latency compression, and temporal opacity. It distinguishes these mechanisms from temporal anticipatory compliance, an emergent behavioral adaptation through which workers reorganize their availability, responsiveness, and temporal boundaries in anticipation of uncertain consequences. By integrating labor process theory, the sociology of time, and sociotechnical systems theory, TSAM explains how computational mediation reconfigures the informational and temporal conditions through which control is exercised, experienced, and contested. The model further theorizes why resource-protective behavior may become less effective when reduced availability carries uncertain consequences, conceptualizes temporal opacity as epistemic asymmetry rather than simple information deficit, and positions resistance as mechanism-specific modification of algorithmic temporal governance. Five propositions translate these theoretical claims into empirically testable and refutable expectations.

items.title: An Agent-Based Model of GenAI in Creative Writing: Novelty Gains and Diversity Declines
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being rapidly adopted in education. Its effects on creativity unfold at both individual and collective levels. We develop an agent-based model that represents students’ creative outputs in a two-dimensional idea space to examine how GenAI assistance in creative writing shapes individual creativity and classroom-level idea diversity. Simulations show that GenAI increases individual creativity, with disproportionately larger gains for less creative students, while reducing collective diversity through idea homogenization. Critically, the model reveals a more nuanced, non-linear pattern of collective diversity than empirical accounts of homogenization alone: collective diversity can increase at low-to-moderate adoption rates before reaching a tipping point and declining at high adoption rates. These findings highlight the need to evaluate GenAI in education using both individual performance metrics and collective system outcomes.

items.abstract: The mining industry is dangerous, with all these accidents happening even though safety rules have gotten better over time. It leads to real tragedies, like people dying on the job. This necessitates adopting advanced Total Quality Management (TQM) practices. This study aims to reduce fatalities by implementing a Plan, Do, Study, Act (PDSA) methodology within the organization to enhance occupational health and safety performance. We gathered data from questionnaires handed out to actual miners, focusing on what causes these deadly accidents, and used a tree diagram as a strategic framework for designing safety interventions and identifying learning pathways. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pareto charts to prioritize high-risk activities. The survey findings suggest that management and leadership commitment, safety training and competency, and safety culture were perceived by respondents as the most important factors influencing safety performance, collectively contributing 61.8% of the impact on safety-related activities. After applying a fishbone diagram analysis, human factors and inadequate maintenance schedules were identified as critical root causes. Overall, The study proposes a PDSA approach to improve Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) performance through TQM practices. items.title: An Overview of Environmental Degradation in Yola South Local Government Area, Adamawa State
items.abstract: This paper aimed to overview environmental degradation in Yola South Local Government Area, Adamawa State. The present paper summarizes pertinent information on environmental degradation in the area through investigating limited available and pertinent studies conducted in the area coupled with field observations and interviews which form the basis of the secondary data for the research. It was identified that drought, flood, soil degradation/erosion and deforestation were the major types of environmental degradation. Similarly, it was also revealed human factor is the most inducing of creating such menace than the natural factor. Loss of properties, lives, destruction of farmlands and buildings, paralysis of socio-economic activities and ecosystems deterioration were among the generated effects caused by the processes of environmental degradation in the area. It is therefore, suggested that government should ensure effective monitoring of the environmental resources and protecting them through formulating and adoption of polices and strategies that will not only safeguard the resources but will also improve and sustain them for future growth and development in the study area.

items.title: Análisis comparativo de la carga mental en el personal administrativo de la Facultad de Ingeniería de la UNACH
items.abstract: Mental workload is one of the main ergonomic risks in today's administrative environments, where psychosocial demands predominate. The objective of this research was to comparatively analyze the mental workload levels of the administrative staff at the Faculty of Engineering of the National University of Chimborazo (UNACH) using the NASA-TLX and SWAT methods, and to determine their relationship with sociodemographic variables. A quantitative, descriptive-correlational, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted with the entire administrative staff (n = 10). Data were processed in SPSS V26 using the chi-square test and Cramér's V coefficient. The results showed a predominance of high mental workload in both instruments (NASA-TLX: 90.0%; SWAT: 60.0%); no statistically significant relationship was found with age or years of experience. These results highlight the importance of implementing psychosocial intervention measures.

items.title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
items.abstract: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. They were selected through an exploratory stakeholder consultation and 3 co-design workshops with audiovisual professionals and participants from organizations supporting people with visual or hearing impairments. They combine conventional TV with complementary content delivered to connected devices, including AR/VR HMD. They were subsequently evaluated through a cross-sectional CAWI survey of 626 Internet and connected TV users in Spain. Each participant viewed standardized video demonstrations of 2 randomly assigned cases and assessed their perceived usefulness, anticipated benefits/limitations, and interest in them. The results show substantial interest across all five use cases, ranging from 64.7% to 76.9%. Adaptive and personalized augmented subtitles received the highest level of interest and were particularly valued for their accessibility, language-learning, and personalization benefits. Immersive services involving complementary AR content, virtual screens, 3D objects, and 360 video were also evaluated positively, although participants identified device cost, ergonomics, connectivity, usability, and synchronization as anticipated limitations. The findings provide user-centered evidence that can inform the prioritization, design, and subsequent prototype-based evaluation of standards-compliant Augmented Hybrid TV services. Because the study assessed video-based scenarios rather than functional systems, the results represent perceived usefulness and stated interest rather than observed adoption or technically validated QoE.

items.title: Autonomous Systems in Transport and Industrial Vehicles: Current Status and Challenges
items.abstract: This narrative review analyses the current state of the art in autonomous systems for road transport and industrial environments (logistics, manufacturing and agriculture). The literature was identified mainly through searches of the Scopus and Web of Science databases (final search: July 2026), complemented by standards and regulatory documents; the search and selection procedure and its limitations are reported. The paper proposes a two-dimensional classification that links the domain of use (industrial and logistics applications, shared mobility on fixed routes and road transport of persons) with the degree of autonomy, using the SAE J3016 levels for on-road vehicles and operational-design-domain descriptions and domain-specific safety frameworks for AGVs, AMRs, drones and agricultural machinery; the technical differences between industrial and road operating environments are compared explicitly. The core technologies are then reviewed and compared: sensing and perception (passive and active sensors, multi-sensor fusion), trajectory planning and decision-making, machine learning and reinforcement learning (including human-in-the-loop approaches), testing, simulation and validation, V2V/V2I/V2X connectivity and ADAS. Comparative tables summarise the evaluation data, metrics, operating conditions and limitations of representative methods; their possible transfer to industrial environments is discussed as a hypothesis that requires industrial validation, not as a demonstrated result. Challenges related to decision-making under uncertainty, ethics, fragmented regulation and human factors, including driver state, emotions and trust, are discussed in relation to the evidence reviewed. Finally, each identified gap is translated into research questions, measurable requirements and validation approaches, and the limits of the review’s coverage are stated.

items.title: Between legal aspiration and engineering reality: technical and legal barriers to implementing control safeguards for high-risk AI systems
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in decisions that affect health, safety, welfare and rights, and regulators have responded by requiring “control safeguards”, such as human oversight, robustness and monitoring, for systems classed as high-risk. This article asks why such safeguards are hard to implement and why the difficulty matters for society. It combines doctrinal analysis of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended in 2026) with a structured critical review of the technical, human-factors and policy literature. Five technical barriers are identified (model opacity, speed and autonomy, brittle guardrails, limits of human attention and judgement, and the lack of tests for control effectiveness), together with six legal and institutional barriers (open-textured legal standards, uncertain classification, delayed standards and guidance, limited regulatory capacity, fragmented enforcement, and burdens on small organisations). The article argues that these barriers reinforce one another through three gaps: a feasibility gap between what the law demands and what technology can deliver, a verification gap between legal requirements and testable criteria, and a capacity gap between large and small actors and between providers and regulators. Mapping each oversight capability in Article 14(4) to these barriers shows where safeguards are most likely to be formal rather than effective. The article proposes ten recommendations for EU institutions, standard-setters, national authorities, providers and deployers, and considers lessons for lower-capacity jurisdictions, including in Africa, that are drawing on EU-style models. The central conclusion is that regulatory attention should shift from documenting oversight to demonstrating that it works.

items.title: Can traditional retail physical shops employ wearable mixed reality in-store?
items.abstract: Purpose The quality of the consumer experience with mixed reality (MR) technology in physical retail environments remains underexplored. The study explores the quality of consumer MR head-mounted display experiences in traditional physical shops and proposes a theoretical framework for understanding space-user behaviours in MR-enabled physical environments. Design/methodology/approach This study uses triangulation and grounded theory to empirically investigate the implementation of an MR Product Configurator app in a UK fashion shop. It derives managerial and design implications for developing MR-enabled shops. Findings The findings suggest that retailers carefully design ergonomic MR environments to improve accessibility of user experience and facilitate adoption. The results address eight factors for interior design (colour, lighting, privacy, safety, sound, merchandise display, spatial dimension, and spatial layout) and four factors for MR system design (interaction design, UI design, system accessibility, and technological stability) for design recommendations to enhance the MR accessibility of physical retail environments. Originality/value An MR customer experience framework is proposed through 68 consumers who adopted an MR headset in-store. The framework depicts the quality of customer experience and current challenges. By addressing these problems, the practical implementation of MR retail may enhance the quality of the experience and accelerate the immersive digitalisation of physical shops.

items.title: Communicating AI-Driven Pollution Intelligence in Environmental Communication, Public Trust, and Real-Time Chemical Pollution Control
items.abstract: AI-driven pollution intelligence is central to environmental governance as chemical pollution is monitored, forecast, visualized, and managed through sensors, IoT systems, predictive analytics, dashboards, citizen-science platforms, and automated alerts. Yet detection alone cannot secure public trust or effective control. This article offers a media-studies and environmental communication analysis of how real-time pollution intelligence can support legitimacy, public understanding, and adaptive action. Based on 30 user-supplied Scopus records, it synthesizes work on AI air-quality monitoring, risk assessment, hazardous chemical vigilance, odour complaints, haze-data contestation, citizen science, health warnings, noise perception, smellscapes, plastic pollution, watershed control, greenwashing, and digital inequality. It argues that pollution intelligence is a sociotechnical communication system requiring data quality, framing, credibility, participation, and response alignment.

items.title: Culinary Knowledge and Skills Performance Among Grade 9 Learners: Basis for Curricular Intervention
items.abstract: Abstract. This study assessed Grade 9 students' culinary knowledge and skills performance at Cookery Agong-ong National High School in Butuan City to inform curricular intervention. Specifically, it examined students' engagement in Cookery in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and safety; assessed their food preparation and plating performance; determined the relationship between student engagement and performance in culinary knowledge and skills; and developed a proposed curricular intervention. The study employed a descriptive-correlational research design. Data were gathered through a structured knowledge test and a performance-based assessment tool anchored on competency standards adapted from TESDA's Cookery NC II framework. The study used percentages, means, standard deviations, and Spearman's rank-order correlation to analyze the data. The findings showed high self-reported student engagement in accuracy (M = 3.82), safety and sanitation (M = 3.77), and efficiency (M = 3.70). Learners also demonstrated excellent performance in preparing tools, equipment, and ingredients (M = 3.79), applying cooking methods and techniques (M = 3.72), kitchen safety and sanitation (M = 3.77), food presentation and plating (M = 3.79), and food storage and packaging (M = 3.68). The study also found a strong, statistically significant positive relationship between student engagement and performance in culinary knowledge and skills (\(\rho = .976, p < .001\)). Based on these findings, the study proposed a Cookery Competency Enhancement Program emphasizing hands-on, competency-based, collaborative, and performance-oriented activities targeting food storage temperature, occupational health and safety, ingredient quality, cooking adaptability, and food presentation. items.title: Decision Time Constraints and Trust Propagation in Multi-Operator Multi-Autonomy Teaming
items.abstract: Modern human–autonomy teams (HATs) often operate under time constraints that limit individuals’ ability to fully evaluate recommendations from the automation and autonomous systems. In these settings, people may rely not only on their own interactions with autonomy, but also on cues from their teammates. This study examines how decision time constraints influence trust propagation in multi-operator, multi-autonomy (MOMA) teams. Participants worked in pairs with two drones in a repeated threat-detection task, making rapid decisions under either standard (3.0 s) or constrained (1.7 s) time conditions. After each round, participants reported their trust in both drones and their teammate, allowing us to quantify how trust propagates based on teammate-reported trust. Results show that trust propagates between teammates in both conditions ( p < . 001), with stronger effects under tighter time constraints (3.0 s: b = 0.29; 1.7 s: b = 0.35). These findings highlight the role of social influences on trust in time-constrained environments and inform the design of human–autonomy systems for high-tempo operations.

items.title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
items.abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At the team level, weighting votes by this pre-emptive neural signal, available before a response is committed, produced substantial accuracy gains on contested (evenly‐split) trials under High Workload (57% to 88% as team size increased from 2 to 16), but was actively detrimental under Low Workload. Discussion Critically, this advantage held even against post‐hoc behavioural signals: confidence was the strongest single team‐level signal overall, but by definition cannot inform a decision still in progress, whereas the neural signal can. These findings indicate that EEG‐based decision‐reliability signals are not a general‐purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload‐conditional one, with clear implications for when and how cBCI systems should be deployed in operational teams.

items.title: Designing Chatbots for Person-Centered Care: Insights from Contraceptive Care in Kenyan Pharmacies
items.abstract: Adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in sub-Saharan Africa face barriers to contraceptive access and lack decision-support resources tailored to their needs. Many Kenyan AGYW seek contraceptive services in the pharmacy setting, but experience stigma, judgment, and privacy concerns that make it difficult to seek guidance from pharmacists. This work examines how chatbots could integrate into Kenya’s pharmacy setting to support AGYW’s contraceptive decision-making. We presented chatbot prototypes in co-design workshops with AGYW and pharmacy workers to evoke reflections on perceived opportunities, concerns, and preferable futures of chatbot-supported care. Our findings highlight expectations that a chatbot could offer private, non-judgmental spaces for information seeking while shifting trust and authority away from pharmacists, revealing tensions surrounding the distribution of authority, reliance, and control among AGYW, pharmacists, and the chatbot. In response to these tensions, we contribute design guidelines for chatbots to navigate community beliefs and promote shared decision-making by AGYW and pharmacists. More broadly, this work extends research on sensitive health chatbots for youth by showing how such tools embedded within a service delivery setting surface distinct considerations for stakeholder roles and person-centered care.

items.title: Directional Bias and Bilateral Symmetry in Thumbstick Control: An Empirical Study of Hand and Target Location Effects
items.abstract: Thumbsticks are widely adopted input devices for gaming, virtual reality, and robot control owing to their simple and intuitive manipulation. However, the kinematic characteristics of thumbstick manipulation within their workspace remain underexplored, given the mismatch between the thumb’s anatomical movement and the device’s two-dimensional analog workspace. We conducted a within-subjects experiment in which 20 participants performed a target-selection task on a commercial gamepad with symmetrical thumbsticks, with targets arranged in two concentric arrays, inner (0.5) and outer (1.0), at eight directions. Endpoint distributions revealed systematic directional biases that varied with target location. While bilateral symmetry was preserved across most target locations, a distinct rotational shift emerged along the vertical axis: clockwise for the left hand and counterclockwise for the right hand. Endpoints at inner targets tended to exceed the 0.5 radius, and participants rated inner-target transitions as the most difficult. These results support direction-aware, cross-hand calibration for thumbsticks.

items.title: Diurnal Variation of Wet Bulb Globe Temperature and Heat Stress Risk During the Wet Season in Port Harcourt, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the diurnal variation of Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) and associated heat stress risk during the wet season in Port Harcourt Metropolis, Rivers State, Nigeria. Hourly WBGT measurements were taken at eight purposively selected sites representing three land use types (urban, peri-urban, and rural) during three representative time blocks (morning: 06:00–09:00, afternoon: 12:00–15:00, and evening: 18:00–21:00) over three non-consecutive days per site between June and August 2026. WBGT was measured using the Heat Index WBGT Meter Model WBGT-2010SD, while supporting meteorological variables were measured using the PCE-FWS 20N mobile weather station. Heat stress risk was classified using three indices: WBGT (ISO 7243), Heat Index (US NWS), and Temperature Humidity Index (THI). Results showed that WBGT ranged from 23.0°C in rural areas to 34.4°C in the urban core. The diurnal pattern was sinusoidal, with a minimum of 24.2°C at 06:00 and a maximum of 32.7°C at 13:00. The peak rate of increase (2.3°C/hour) occurred between 07:00 and 09:00, and WBGT exceeded 30.0°C for seven consecutive hours (09:00–15:00). Extreme heat stress risk (WBGT ≥ 32.0°C) occurred for three hours (12:00–14:00). All three indices identified the early afternoon as the period of greatest heat stress. The study concludes that heat stress is a significant hazard during the wet season in Port Harcourt, particularly during the early afternoon. The findings provide the first systematic, hourly WBGT dataset for the city and offer an empirical basis for occupational health policies, public health advisories, and climate change adaptation strategies. To address the findings of the study, the study recommended that outdoor work should be scheduled to avoid the peak heat stress period between 09:00 and 15:00; heat advisories should be issued during the early afternoon, when WBGT is highest; environmental regulatory agencies, develop heat-health action plans, workplace heat regulations, and climate adaptation strategies; and continuous 24-hour WBGT monitoring should be carried out to capture night-time conditions.

items.title: Do what you want to do: an analysis of positive mental health literacy among pre-service teachers at a regional university in China
items.abstract: Positive mental health literacy (PMHL) is an important resource for promoting psychological wellbeing and resilience. Research on teachers’ mental health literacy has, however, concentrated on the recognition of mental illness among in-service teachers; its positive dimension has rarely been examined among pre-service teachers, and never in relation to their motivation for entering the profession. This study investigated the level of PMHL among pre-service teachers, examined differences in PMHL across demographic and background characteristics, and explored their perceptions of factors related to positive mental health. A convergent mixed-methods design was adopted, and data were collected from 455 pre-service teachers at a regional teacher-education university in Hunan Province, China, using a questionnaire comprising demographic items, a PMHL scale, and four open-ended questions. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t -tests, and one-way ANOVA, while qualitative data were analysed through thematic analysis. The findings showed that pre-service teachers demonstrated a generally high level of PMHL ( M = 3.78, SD = 0.67). Statistically significant differences were found according to year of study, gender and career motivation, and career motivation was associated with the largest effect (η 2 = 0.086), followed by year of study (η 2 = 0.029) and gender ( d = −0.34). A small difference by major (η 2 = 0.024, p = 0.049) did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and is reported as tentative. No significant differences were observed for admission pathway, age, family background, or teaching practicum experience. Qualitative findings revealed that employment and future competition pressure were the most frequently reported sources of stress, whereas leisure activities, social support, personal goals, and life adjustment were commonly identified as factors supporting positive mental health. Because the design is cross-sectional, these results describe associations rather than causal pathways, and they characterize pre-service teachers at one regional university rather than in China as a whole. Within these limits, the findings highlight the importance of strengthening pre-service teachers’ intrinsic motivation for teaching, so that their learning is driven more by interest, purpose, and positive psychological engagement.

items.title: Earthquake early warning as a socio-technical system: a cross-country systematic literature review
items.abstract: Earthquake Early Warning systems have expanded, yet their effectiveness depends on technical performance and whether warnings prompt timely protective action. This systematic review examines interactions among technical, institutional, and behavioural dimensions across EEW contexts. Following PRISMA 2020, literature published between 1975 and August 2026 was searched using Scopus and Massey University Library Discover. Of 1,202 records, 62 studies met the inclusion criteria. Evidence was synthesised across eight jurisdictions: Japan, Mexico, Taiwan, the United States, Aotearoa New Zealand, Switzerland, China, and Israel. Comparisons considered system maturity, technical architecture, public exposure, and differences among retrospective reports of alert responses, experiment, and stated intentions. EEW was generally perceived as valuable for situational awareness and psychological preparedness, but immediate protective action remained inconsistent. System maturity, alert thresholds, governance, risk communication, public knowledge, and preparedness practices were associated with variation in the warning-to-action pathway. Familiarity with established systems did not necessarily translate into protective action, highlighting the importance of context-specific guidance, institutional clarity, preparedness training, and accessible communication. The findings frame EEW as a socio-technical system in which technical capability creates the opportunity for protective action, while institutional, social, and behavioural conditions influence how that opportunity is used and may contribute to risk reduction.

items.title: Effects of Explanations on Driver Situation Awareness Under Physical Adversarial Attacks in Automated Driving: A Driving Simulator Study
items.abstract: As automated driving systems (ADS) become increasingly integrated into real-world transportation, understanding how human drivers perceive and respond to system failures under adversarial conditions is critical for driving safety. Prior research has shown that human drivers overestimate ADS capabilities and lack awareness of ADS vulnerability to adversarial attacks. We conduct a laboratory study (N=32) using a driving simulator, investigating the effectiveness of explanations on enhancing human drivers' situation awareness (SA) of physical adversarial evasion attacks and their takeover performance in SAE Level 3 automated driving. We varied system reliability and attack object within subjects and explanation between subjects. Quantitative results indicated that explanations enhanced drivers' SA, without deteriorating their takeover performance. The reliability manipulation yielded non-significant results in general, probably because of explanatory content presented for the ADS detected-and-handled attacks. Nevertheless, we obtained the impact of attack object on drivers' takeover control regardless of the explanation manipulation. Qualitative results revealed that drivers often noticed abnormalities without recognizing them as attacks, while perceiving explanations as useful aids for understanding scenarios. We discuss implications of our findings and directions of future work.

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Cyber Resilience: A Call for Comprehensive Training and Regulation
items.abstract: This article addresses the critical issues associated with maritime cyber-security and focusses on the training and education needed for maritime sector employees and professionals in the port sector. It provides essential context for understanding the increasing threat landscape, exemplified by a 900 per cent rise in cyber breaches targeting operational technology in ships and ports in 2023. It underscores the global impact of cyber threats, and highlights major incidents in ports worldwide. The escalating frequency of attacks on shipping lines, container terminals and national key points raises concerns about financial losses and potential risks to human life, alongside damage to infrastructure and the environment. We argue that the critical aspect of cyber resilience is the human factor, which is considered to be a potential weak link in cyber-security. We explore the importance of training the maritime workforce to enhance cyber resilience, analyse the scope of the training obligations imposed by the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code, and note gaps in the application of this framework in South Africa's Merchant Shipping (Maritime Security) Regulations, 2004. Furthermore, the non-mandatory guidelines to the ISPS Code lack both force of law and sufficient specificity. Against this background we emphasise the growing attention by regulators in the United States, European Union and United Kingdom to the vulnerabilities of cyber-physical systems in ports, and the need for specific regulations to address these risks. While acknowledging the existing regulations, we advocate the urgent development of a comprehensive port-sector cyber-security policy and guidelines in South Africa and the amendment of the existing regulations to include mandatory cyber-security provisions. In conclusion we emphasise the need for a coordinated effort in the South African port sector to promote cyber resiliency, understood as being the ability to identify, mitigate and respond to cyber threats effectively. We call for the integration of cyber-security into executive strategies, policies and procedures, and stress the importance of continuous learning and information sharing to create a resilient maritime industry.

items.title: Evaluating Public Plans for AI Systems: Comparing Premortem and Promortems
items.abstract: Effective planning requires anticipating risks before they occur, yet planners often underestimate potential failures due to optimism bias. This research compared three reasoning techniques—critique, premortem, and promortem—for evaluating a proposed automated high-speed rail plan across two experiments (individual, N = 108; group, N = 30). Participants rated their confidence and understanding of the plan before and after generating reasons, then generated potential solutions. Premortem reasoning reduced participants’ confidence in the plan and then supported confidence recovery once solutions were generated, whereas promortem reasoning increased confidence throughout the session, consistent with optimism bias; effects were more pronounced in group settings. Critique and premortem elicited a higher proportion of reasons and solutions related to the plan’s AI than promortem. Findings support the premortem as a tool for calibrating confidence and generating actionable, domain-relevant risks during early-stage technology planning.

items.title: Examining English Learning Demotivation Level of Indonesian First-Year University Students: A Comparative Study
items.abstract: Demotivation can undermine students’ engagement and persistence in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, particularly during the transition to university, when first-year students encounter new academic and assessment demands. Understanding its sources is therefore important for supporting students’ adjustment and sustained engagement in English learning. The current study aimed to investigate the level of students’ demotivation in English learning, the dominant factors, and the differences based on gender and educational background. It focused on first-year students enrolled in an Islamic University in Madura that considers English as a compulsory and intensive course. This study was a quantitative research with a survey design. Demotivation questionnaires were adopted and modified from Sakai and Kikuchi (2009) and administered to 147 students through Google Forms. The findings revealed a moderate level of demotivation. Based on the reverse scale, in which lower scores indicate higher demotivation, test scores emerged as the most prominent demotivating factor (M = 3.03), followed by inadequate learning facilities (M = 3.16), learning contents and materials (M = 3.31), lack of intrinsic motivation (M = 3.33), and teacher competence and teaching styles (M = 3.50). A significant gender difference was found, with male students reporting higher demotivation (M = 3.10) than female students (M = 3.39), t(145) = 2.134, p = .035. In contrast, no significant difference was found across educational backgrounds, F(5, 141) = 1.068, p = .381. These findings highlight the importance of assessment experiences in first-year EFL demotivation and suggest the need for more supportive assessment practices during students’ transition to university English learning..

items.title: External resilience controls as sociotechnical governance: an extension of dynamic capabilities theory under externally driven volatility
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organizations construct governance responses to externally driven volatility by embedding external signals into control practices. Focusing on climate exposed agricultural firms, this study extends dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) by developing external resilience controls (ERCs) as a sociotechnical governance construct that illuminates how firms make volatility actionable through formal control routines. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a pragmatic constructivist design science orientation, this study combines six years of financial and operational context (2019–2024) with a longitudinal interpretive content analysis of annual report and sustainability disclosures (2022–2024) from five major agricultural firms. An interpretive design approach enables the systematic synthesis of disclosed organizational practices into a conceptual framework. Findings ERCs emerge as sociotechnical governance arrangements that translate external volatility into organizationally meaningful routines and actionable dynamic capabilities. These arrangements materialize through digital sensing infrastructures, traceability systems, scenario thresholds and board-level oversight that collectively shape how firms interpret and respond to climate anomalies, regulatory shifts and technological change. ERCs reveal resilience as an ongoing process of constructing, stabilizing and legitimizing responses to external volatility. Practical implications ERCs offer practitioners an analytic framework to operationalize dynamic capabilities by integrating digital tools and governance structures. They show how firms convert external volatility into actionable sensing, seizing and reconfiguring routines, enabling adaptive decision-making without relying on rigid control mechanisms. Originality/value This study advances qualitative management scholarship by conceptualizing ERCs as sociotechnical governance constructs. It contributes to strategy research by extending DCT, showing how dynamic capabilities are enacted through the interplay of digital infrastructures, institutional pressures, and organizational sensemaking.

items.title: From hobbies to examination progression: a study of art-track candidates' motivations for participating in non-academic tutoring
items.abstract: Non-academic tutoring is an important channel through which families help their children accumulate cultural capital. Existing studies have mostly analysed parental motivations from a static perspective, and few have examined how students' motivations change across educational stages. Based on in-depth interviews with 22 art-track candidates, this article finds that their motivations for participating in arts tutoring show a marked shift from value rationality to instrumental rationality. In primary school and before, the intrinsic motivation of personal interest dominated their participation in interest classes. At the two key educational transitions of the high school entrance examination (zhongkao) and the college entrance examination (gaokao), they chose to study art majors out of the extrinsic motivation of examination progression. In this process, the form of tutoring they attended shifted from arts interest classes to professional intensive training classes, and the learning content was replaced by examination subjects for art majors.

items.title: From technology to meaningful learning: cognitive, communicative, and cross-cultural effects of AI integration in bilingual education
items.abstract: Background Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in bilingual education is increasingly consequential for students' cognitive engagement and professional communication, yet prior research has examined these outcomes largely in isolation. Whether learning engagement and cross-cultural competence (CCC) operate as simultaneous, parallel indirect pathways linking AI integration to perceived learning effectiveness and business communication skill remains underexamined, and cultural intelligence has rarely been modeled as a boundary condition on the intercultural pathway. Methods Drawing on a cross-sectional dataset of 604 bilingual education students across 13 universities in China, this study integrated the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, Social Cognitive Theory, and Cultural Intelligence Theory within a single framework. Ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors and partial least squares structural equation modeling with bootstrap-based indirect effect and latent moderation analyses were employed. Results All three indirect pathways were statistically supported: AI → learning engagement → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.191), AI → CCC → business communication skill (β = 0.278), and AI → CCC → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.202), each carrying a larger share of the AI-outcome association than the corresponding direct path. The model explained 28.38% of variance in learning engagement, 34.33% in CCC, 40.85% in business communication skill, and 47.28% in perceived learning effectiveness. Cultural intelligence positively moderated the AI → CCC association (β = 0.200), with simple slopes rising from 0.298 at low cultural intelligence to 0.697 at high cultural intelligence. Conclusion AI integration is associated with distal learning and communication outcomes predominantly through engagement-related and intercultural mechanisms, with cultural intelligence conditioning the strength of the intercultural pathway. These findings suggest that AI funding in bilingual education should be conditioned on process metrics, learning engagement and intercultural capability, rather than on tool procurement alone. Structured intercultural scaffolding should be required as an accreditation condition for AI-supported bilingual courses, and cultural intelligence screening at program entry with tiered support for lower-cultural-intelligence learners warrants consideration, given that the benefits of AI-supported learning are non-uniform across learners.

items.title: Geometric Properties of Human High-Performing Buildings: A Review of the Evidence and the Implications for Practice
items.abstract: Building performance is conventionally assessed in structural, thermal, energy, and functional terms, while architectural character is treated as a matter of taste. Yet a growing body of research suggests that the geometric characteristics of buildings also affect performance experienced directly by people—perceptual engagement, restoration and well-being, perceived safety, social affordance, and patterns of movement and use—both within buildings and in adjoining streets and public spaces. This paper reviews that evidence and develops a conceptual model and theoretical account of how the relevant characteristics arise. Drawing on environmental psychology, experimental aesthetics, neuroaesthetics, urban design, and the mathematics of form, it identifies recurring geometric characteristics associated with favorable human responses, centered on symmetry and symmetry-breaking, multiscale organization, and contextual relationship. It proposes that these are traces of generative processes rather than attributes of style, and it introduces “deep symmetry”: a progression of correspondence from the isolated object through scale and context to the perceiving human participant, with a candidate mechanism grounded in embodied perception and processing fluency. The framework reframes stylistic debates as questions of human performance, geometry, and process, and sets out a falsifiable research agenda, candidate measures, and broader implications for practice.

items.abstract: Green empowerment of employees is increasingly recognized as a key strategy in the hotel industry, supporting sustainable business models and corporate social responsibility. However, hotels in emerging economies, such as Ethiopia, often face criticism for poor environmental performance. Using self-determination theory, this study developed a hybrid framework to examine the impact of green empowerment on the proactive environmental behaviors of employees in Ethiopian five-star hotels. Analysis of 305 usable questionnaires revealed that intrinsic motivation, competency, and recognition significantly enhance these proactive behaviors, highlighting the importance of fostering a supportive hotel ecosystem that values employee engagement in green practices.

items.title: Guided Immersive Virtual Reality for Flooding-Response Training in Commercial Fishing
items.abstract: Commercial fishing is among the world’s most hazardous occupations, yet classroom-based safety training provides limited opportunities to practice responding to rare, life-threatening emergencies such as vessel flooding. This paper presents an immersive virtual reality (VR) flooding-response training module built in Unreal Engine and examines whether embedded instructional guidance improves trainee performance and user experience. A between-subjects study (N = 16) compared guided VR, featuring contextual text prompts displayed near interactive objects, with unguided VR. Participants in the guided condition reportedsignificantly greater usability and immersion and significantly lower cognitive load than those in the unguided condition (all W = 0, p < .05). They also completed the flooding-response task significantly faster (t(7) = 2.14, p = .034, one-tailed). These preliminary findings suggest that instructional scaffolding embedded withinVR simulations may improve the usability and training effectiveness of high-risk safety training. Guided VR may therefore offer a promising complement to traditional drill-based programs.

items.title: Hegemonic Masculinity, Motivation and Aggression Among Collegiate Male Athletes: A Quantitative Correlational Study
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship among hegemonic masculinity, sports motivation, and aggression among collegiate male athletes in the satellite campuses of Bukidnon State University. Specifically, it determined the level of adherence to hegemonic masculinity in terms of emotional control, self-reliance, risk-taking, winning, and heterosexual self-presentation; assessed sports motivation based on intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and amotivation; and identified aggression in sports through behavioral and emotional aggression. The study employed a quantitative correlational research design involving 53 male collegiate athletes selected through purposive sampling. Data were gathered using adopted and validated survey instruments, including measures of masculine norms, sports motivation, and aggression. Descriptive statistics and correlational analysis were utilized to analyze the data and determine the relationships among variables. The findings revealed that masculine identity, motivational factors, and aggressive tendencies are interconnected aspects of athletes’ experiences. The study highlighted that competitive orientations and certain masculine expectations may influence athletes’ emotional regulation and behavioral responses during sports participation. The results provided empirical evidence for developing a gender-sensitive intervention program focused on promoting healthy masculinity, self-determined motivation, emotional regulation, sportsmanship, and responsible athletic behavior. The study contributes to understanding the psychological and social factors shaping male collegiate athletes within a local sports context.

items.title: Hopes and fears: first year geoscience students encounter with academia
items.abstract: Through interviews and questionnaires, we investigate geoscience students’ motivations, expectations and concerns at the start of the bachelor programme at the University of Oslo, Norway, and how these change as the students encounter the courses, peers, staff and study environment in their first year. Students begin with a mix of extrinsic and intrinsic motivations that become more self-determined over the first year. Initially, they are eager to learn but unsure they can succeed; by year’s end doubts shift toward the applicability of their education and future job prospects. Students hope to build relationships and make friends and fear that they will not; although these fears subside quickly for most, students consistently emphasize the importance of positive relationships. Though greater self-determination and better relationships typically are viewed as something positive, for some students it appears that increased self-determination is accompanied by heightened sensitivity to academic difficulties, teacher expectations, and the implications of success or failure. Though institutional shortcomings were not cited as reasons for dropping out by participants in this study, the findings highlight opportunities to support student success and retention by addressing self-efficacy, study technique, perceived relevance, and workload management.

items.title: How Distributed, Consensus-Free Folklore Enables Transfeminine Disposability on Bluesky
items.abstract: Bluesky, a novel social networking platform, offers a space with valuable community ties for transfeminine individuals. At the same time, though, these communities are not free of intracommunity conflict, particularly conflict predicated on a transmisogynistic politics of disposability. We conduct a grounded theory interview study with 13 transfeminine Bluesky users, finding that transfeminine individuals experience attacks predicated on their disposability that are primarily driven by a form of disinformation we call distributed, consensus-free (DCF) folklore. DCF folklore turns communities against users who have previously provided crucial labor to those same communities; we frame it as an networked phenomenon that results from extant dynamics and affordances on the platform. In order to mitigate the harms done by the circulation of this folklore, we conclude by discussing opportunities for tools to more effectively support bottom-up moderation that affords for nuance and contextualization.

items.title: How Filial Piety Shapes Benefit Finding Among Family Caregivers: A Narrative Study Based on Adult Child Caregivers of Older Parents With Dementia
items.abstract: This narrative study explored how Chinese filial piety influences benefit finding among adult child caregivers of parents with dementia in Shanghai. Through in-depth interviews with 15 adult child caregivers of parents predominantly living with moderate dementia, we identified filial piety's dual role: It strengthened caregivers' role identity and moral responsibility, inspiring intrinsic motivation that enhanced benefit finding while reshaping intergenerational authority. This transformation guided caregivers to balance familial obligations with personal development in medical, daily care, and institutional care decisions, reinterpreting filial ethics through informed caregiving and emotional connection. By balancing parental well-being, filial responsibility, and caregiver sustainability, participants reconstructed filial piety through meaningful companionship, intergenerational responsibility, and self-care. This reflected an evolution from compliant filial piety to balanced filial piety. These findings highlight how culture shapes benefit finding, with implications for dementia family support that honors ethical traditions while meeting contemporary needs.

items.title: How is Work-Related Fatigue Defined and Measured in Anaesthesiology, Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine? A Scoping Review Protocol
items.abstract: Fatigue among clinical staff working in anaesthesiology, intensive care and emergency medicine is widely regarded as a determinant of both patient safety and staff well-being. Shift work, night duty and on-call commitments are structural features of these specialties, and the resulting sleep loss and circadian disruption are consistently discussed as sources of impaired performance, reduced vigilance and adverse occupational health outcomes. Despite this attention, the literature does not converge on a single operationalisation of the construct. Fatigue is variously described as a subjective state, a performance decrement, a consequence of sleep debt, or a dimension of burnout, and it is assessed with instruments that were developed for different purposes and different populations. Subjective questionnaires, objective psychomotor testing, actigraphy and qualitative accounts coexist in the same body of literature, frequently without explicit justification for the chosen approach. Terms such as fatigue, sleepiness and emotional exhaustion are used interchangeably in some reports and as distinct constructs in others. This heterogeneity limits comparability across studies and complicates the design of interventional research. A scoping review is the appropriate design here because the objective is to map the conceptual and methodological landscape rather than to estimate the effect of a defined intervention on a defined outcome. Consistent with JBI guidance, no critical appraisal of individual sources is planned, as the aim is to characterise the breadth of definitions and measurement approaches in use, not to grade the strength of evidence.

items.title: Idealizing energy democracy in the European semi-periphery: lithium mining, solar energy and fiction
items.abstract: Abstract Background The EU Green Deal aims to turn Europe into the first carbon neutral continent by 2050. However, criticisms of the hegemonic versions of this energy transition have focused on the top-down, asymmetric and corporate dimensions that often view local communities as barriers to the swift implementation of renewable energy infrastructures. Indeed, current scholarship argues that the energy transition is only maximizing the contradictions of neoliberal capitalism as the rapid rollout of green technologies increases North/South asymmetries, thereby fostering capital accumulation, green grabbing and ecocide. Research findings have furthermore argued that semi-peripheral countries such as Portugal are disproportionately affected by these negative impacts of the EU Green Deal. This paper explores two of the leading environmental controversies in the Portuguese context stemming directly from the prevailing energy transition – lithium mining in northern Portugal and plans to construct a large solar power plant in the Alentejo. Results The controversial lithium mining and solar energy projects prioritise corporate ownership, the centralization of renewable energy production, the marginalization of local communities as well as producing large green sacrifice zones and raising issues around energy democracy. This paper explores the role of fiction in the idealization of counter-hegemonic alternatives to the energy transition in keeping with the energy democracy theoretical framework. Highlighting some of the main principles of energy democracy – such as democratic control over energy systems, the redistribution of political-economic power, the universal right to renewable energy and social justice – this article puts forward a fictional scenario, set in 2035, in an ecovillage in Central Portugal. Through exploring the ways in which this fictional community put its own energy transition into practice, the paper sketches a speculative future aligned with the theoretical and sociopolitical concerns around energy democracy. Conclusion Our research suggests fiction might support the imagination of utopian versions of energy futures, articulating energy democracy principles with specific sociotechnical endeavours, problematizing the climate realism underpinning the predominant energy transitions. In this sense, fiction may play an important role in idealizing democratic energy transitions, combining the “what if” of socio-literary techniques with the normative demands and contradictions of low-carbon futures.

items.title: Impact of Environments
items.abstract: This chapter examines the ways physical, virtual, and natural environments shape mental health, occupational participation, and overall well-being. Drawing on occupational therapy models such as MOHO, PEO, CMOP-E, the Kawa Model, and the Ecology of Human Performance, it highlights the dynamic relationship between individuals, their environments, and everyday occupations. The chapter explores how the built environment—including housing, community spaces, and universal design—can either support or constrain participation, while emphasizing the importance of respecting personal meaning, culture, and choice in environmental adaptation. It also addresses the growing influence of virtual environments, considering both the benefits of digital access and telehealth and the risks associated with digital exclusion and technology overuse. The role of the natural environment is examined through evidence on green space, animals, gardening, and adventure-based experiences as contexts for promoting regulation, resilience, and connection. Through case illustrations and practical assessment tools, the chapter demonstrates how occupational therapists analyze and adapt environments to reduce occupational deprivation and promote justice, safety, and dignity. Environmental sustainability and advocacy are framed as emerging responsibilities within contemporary occupational therapy practice.

items.title: Interactive Multimedia for Accounting Education: A Conceptual Framework for Student Engagement and Perceived Learning Outcomes of Gamified Learning Modules
items.abstract: The increasing integration of interactive multimedia into higher education has created opportunities to enhance teaching and learning experiences, including in accounting education, where students must develop conceptual understanding and apply accounting principles to various learning situations. Gamified learning modules offer an engaging approach by incorporating interactive activities and game elements into the learning process. However, evaluating their educational value requires consideration not only of students’ participation but also of their perceptions, engagement, and perceived learning outcomes. This study aims to examine students’ perceptions of implemented gamified learning modules and explore their relationships with behavioural, emotional, and cognitive engagement, as well as perceived learning outcomes in accounting education. The proposed conceptual framework positions students’ perceptions of gamified learning as an important dimension associated with their engagement and perceived learning experiences. Positive perceptions are expected to correspond with higher engagement, while stronger engagement is proposed to be associated with more favourable perceived learning outcomes. These relationships provide a foundation for examining how students experience gamified accounting activities beyond the immediate appeal of interactive features. The study contributes to accounting education literature by integrating student perceptions, multidimensional engagement, and perceived learning outcomes within a single conceptual framework. It also distinguishes perceived learning outcomes from objective academic achievement, recognising that students’ evaluations of their learning experiences do not necessarily indicate improvements in examination performance. Practically, the proposed framework may assist accounting educators in evaluating existing gamified learning practices, identifying dimensions of student engagement that warrant attention, and aligning interactive multimedia activities with intended learning objectives. Ultimately, the study emphasises the importance of pedagogical purpose in gamification, positioning interactive multimedia not merely as a technological enhancement but as a learning approach whose educational value should be considered in relation to students’ engagement and perceived learning experiences

items.title: INTERDISCIPLINARY INTEGRATION IN COMPUTER SCIENCE LESSONS
items.abstract: The practical significance of this study lies in the detailed description of the didactic conditions under which Excel-based digital tools can be effectively used to overcome formalism in students' knowledge acquisition. By examining the interdisciplinary integration of mathematics, geography, and computer science, the study demonstrates how abstract mathematical concepts, including formulas, functions, and percentages, as well as complex geographical indicators such as temperature and precipitation patterns, can be transformed into interactive visual representations within the Excel environment. Such an approach promotes visual-spatial thinking, increases students' intrinsic motivation and cognitive engagement, and facilitates the transition from rote memorization to meaningful experimentation and independent knowledge construction.

items.title: Is gig work the same for everyone? Psychosocial job demands, resources, and well-being in platform work across Europe: evidence from the GIG-OSH study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Research on digital platform work increasingly highlights unclear employment arrangements and pressures related to algorithmic management. This study aimed to describe psychosocial working conditions in web-based and on-location gig work using the job demands‑resources (JD-R) model and examine associations between job demands, job resources, factors preventing resource depletion (FPRD), and health outcomes among platform workers. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Cross-sectional data were drawn from the GIG-OSH project conducted in 7 European countries (Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom). Data were collected through an online survey in November 2023 - April 2024. The analytic sample comprised 3299 platform workers (1476 on-location, 1823 web-based). A project-specific questionnaire assessed socio-demographic characteristics, employment conditions, workload, occupational safety and health hazards, psychosocial working conditions, algorithmic management, and health outcomes. Psychosocial factors were classified as job demands, job resources, or FPRD within an extended JD-R framework. RESULTS: Platform work was characterized by an imbalance between job demands and resources, particularly among onlocation workers. Compared with web-based workers, they reported greater exposure to emotionally disturbing situations, aggression, violence, discrimination, and sexual harassment. Working alone was common in both groups but more prevalent in web-based work. Factors preventing resource depletion indicators, especially absence of fines and protection against fraudulent bookings, were more favourable in web-based work. Higher job demands were significantly associated with poorer health outcomes, with emotionally disturbing situations showing the strongest effect. Job resources demonstrated modest protective associations, whereas FPRD indicators, particularly not working while ill, were consistently associated with better health. CONCLUSIONS: Platform work involves substantial psychosocial risks linked to poorer well-being and health, supporting the JD-R model. items.title: Linking Team Situation Awareness Through Verbal Communication Patterns
items.abstract: Team Situation Awareness (TSA), a collective understanding of changes in the surroundings, is critical in human-human teaming in dynamic settings. Team members maintain their TSA through continuous verbal communication, yet little is known about how communication is associated with TSA. This study investigated the association between TSA and communication patterns across SA levels and dimensions (environment, task, and team) in a construction setting. Twenty-one dyads (42 people) completed a two-worker-cobot pipe task in a VR construction site. Participants collaboratively performed an interdependent pipe task while monitoring potential hazards, task progress, and teammates’ status. Communication was analyzed using the speech act coding framework, and TSA was assessed using the SAGAT survey, serving as ground truth. The results show that high TSA dyads generated more level 2 environmental communication and demonstrated a more balanced communication pattern between participants. The results advance understanding of communication in TSA, and support communication-based algorithms for at-risk workers.
